title: Orchestrated tool tunnel: token-budget-aware feedback throttles and compatibility shims
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: Multi-tool chains in the Core API increasingly run into two classes of failures in production: (1) runaway recursive invocation patterns where a tool's output is re-ingested and subsequently re-triggers the same tool multiple times, and (2) incompatibilities between legacy tool outputs (freeform text / HTML snippets) and the new structured-output contract. Both cause latency spikes, increased token cost, and occasional incorrect state transitions in the orchestrator.

Goal: Implement an "orchestrated tool tunnel" that provides: a) lightweight, token-budget-aware recursion guards (soft and hard limits), b) feedback throttles that rate-limit tool reinvocation based on provenance + recent-effect score, c) a compatibility shim layer that normalizes legacy outputs into our structured-output contract (JSON schema + metadata), and d) stream-friendly result injection markers so streamed responses can indicate whether injected tool results are authoritative, provisional, or truncated.

Why now: We observed two production incidents (internal incident-2026-02-11-T01 and spike on 2026-02-19) where recursive chains inflated token usage by 3-5x. Customers using function-calling plus streaming (chat + tool chain) reported inconsistent UI behavior when a tool returned HTML or markdown instead of our expected structured object. Fixing this reduces cost, improves UX, and prevents inadvertent infinite loops from user-provided tools or third-party connectors.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator enforces soft recursion threshold (per-request per-tool) configurable via route config (default: 3 re-invocations) and hard ceiling that terminates with a clear structured error.
Feedback throttle uses rolling window of recent side-effects (writes, external calls) to decide permitted reinvocations; documented and test-covered policy behavior.

Compatibility shim successfully converts at least three legacy output patterns (HTML blob, freeform text with embedded JSON, deprecated key-value strings) into the structured-output schema with confidence scores.

Streaming responses include result-injection markers: {"injection_state": "authoritative|provisional|truncated", "provenance_id": <id>} embedded as separate streamed events and validated in e2e tests.
No regression in existing streaming latency SLOs (>99th percentile increase <5% for matched workloads).
Documentation and console UI surfaces (per-route settings) updated to show recursion limits and compatibility shim opt-outs.
Feature flag gated rollout and canary to 10% of tenants in dedicated mode before global enablement.
technical_notes: Recursion guard design: maintain per-request call stack fingerprint (sha256 of tool id + input signature) and per-tool counter with TTL tied to request lifecycle. Soft threshold sends a warning event and returns a provisional injection marker; hard threshold returns a structured error with 'recursion_halting' code.

Token-budget awareness: associate budget metadata with each request (configurable via API header X-Token-Budget). Budget exhausted -> choose between truncating tool response (with 'truncated' marker) or rejecting new tool invocations depending on route policy.

Feedback throttle: compute side-effect score from side-effect events (db writes, outbound webhooks, file ops). Use exponentially weighted moving average (alpha=0.3) over 60s window. If score > threshold, restrict re-invocations for that tool for the request and emit telemetry metric 'tool.reinvoke_blocked'.

Compatibility shim: pipeline of heuristics: (1) content-type header mapping, (2) detect embedded JSON via regex and validate against structured schema, (3) HTML -> text extraction + attempt to parse key:value patterns, (4) heuristic confidence score propagated. Keep original raw output in provenance store for audit.

Streaming markers: use an out-of-band event stream chunk with tag 'INJECTION_META' that the client SDK will expose as a structured event. This avoids polluting human-visible token stream. SDKs must be updated to surface the marker in onEvent callbacks.

Graceful fallback: when shim fails to normalize, return original output with 'provisional' marker and a shim_failure_reason in metadata. Also surface a rerun suggestion for the user to call tool with 'best_effort_normalize=true'.
Compatibility layer must be pluggable: customers with strict legacy behavior can opt-out per-route via route config 'compat_shim: off'.
test_plan: Unit tests for fingerprinting and counter increment/decrement semantics (edge: parallel forks and merge).
Property tests that multiple distinct inputs produce different fingerprints and do not collide under normal workload.
E2E test that simulates a 5-step recursive loop and verifies soft/hard cutoffs and telemetry emitted.
Load test (k6) to ensure streaming marker injection doesn't increase CPU per-request by >10% and 99th percentile latency remains within acceptable bounds.
Compatibility shim fuzzing against corpus of 2k legacy tool outputs collected from staging connectors.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag behind 'orchestrated_tool_tunnel'. Start with internal-only canary for infra/SE accounts.
Canary phase: 10% Dedicated tenants + 5 internal production namespaces for 72 hours, monitor 'tool.reinvoke_blocked', 'shim.failure_rate', and latency SLOs.
Expand to 50% if metrics stable for 7 days, then full rollout. Support rollback via flag and one-click rollback runbook.
Post-rollout: run a 14-day telemetry audit to validate cost savings and loop prevention efficacy.
comments: 2026-02-28 - Aisha Patel: Initial spike analysis looks like 60% of recursive invocations came from a single customer connector that returns HTML blobs. Adding that connector to the fuzz corpus now.
2026-03-03 - Olivia Martinez (PM): Confirmed with support that three customers reported UI glitches when HTML arrived mid-stream. PM wants shim as opt-in by default, not opt-out.
2026-03-06 - Review: Security reviewed shim plan; no secrets retained but recommended adding explicit consent for storing raw outputs for provenance. Security note added to tech notes.
2026-03-09 - Liam Chen: Prototype implemented for fingerprinting and streaming event tag. Proof-of-concept canary passed internal smoke tests with small overhead.
2026-03-12 - Design (Eve Tan): SDK event semantics approved; we need to coordinate a minor SDK release to surface INJECTION_META events before canary.
2026-03-14 - Aisha Patel: PRs opened for orchestrator core and js/sdk. Beginning integration tests; observed shim failure rate ~2.1% on staging corpus (acceptable threshold 5%).
decisions: Embed injection markers as out-of-band streaming events rather than in-token JSON to avoid corrupting natural language outputs.
Default behavior: compat_shim=on for hosted API, on for Dedicated; allow per-route opt-out. Rationale: majority of customers prefer stable structured outputs.
Soft vs hard recursion thresholds: soft default=3, hard default=6. Make configurable per-tenant via plan-level guardrails.
Store raw outputs in encrypted provenance store for 30 days; audit log entry whenever shim modifies output.
